segments.text: In this video,

we will explore the management
of documents and panels in Altium Designer

highlighting how documents and panels
are used to organize and manage

the design workspace
in Altium Designer.

Right-click on any document
in the document bar
and select Tile All in the pop-up menu.

The currently open documents
will be split into individual windows.

While documents are tiled or split
within the editing workspace,

right-click on any document
in the document bar

and select Merge All
from the pop-up menu.

The workspace will be restored
to a single document display.

Other options in the right-click menu
include split vertically
and horizontally.
For multi-monitor display,

click on Open In New Window
within the right-click menu

to open a new instance or simply drag
a document to the secondary display.

Locate the Panels button
in the lower right corner.

This shows all the available panels
for the active document type.

Select Properties
from the pop-up menu
to open the Properties panel.

Panels are also listed in the View menu,
under Panels.

Three different display modes
are supported for panels:
docked,
pop-up,
and floating.
For the docked panel display mode,

right-click on the title bar
of the Projects panel.

Click on Allow Dock
in the pop-up menu

and ensure that it is enabled
for horizontally and vertically.
While holding the left-click,
drag the panel to the center of the window
and notice that while the panel is

we have both horizontal
and vertical docking options.

Hover the cursor above the left docking
option and release the left-click hold.

Locate the Components panel tab
on the right of the window.

The Components panel
may need to be opened manually

by clicking on the Panels button
in the lower right.

By default, this panel will open
in the pop-up panel display mode.
Hover over its tab to open the panel.

This mode is what we refer to as
“pop-up mode”

and is often used to
maximize screen real estate,

especially when working
on a small monitor.

To change the Components panel
to docked mode,

click on the pin symbol
while the panel is open.

The pin symbol will change to indicate
that it's in docked mode.
Selecting the pin symbol again

will change the panel
back to pop-up mode.
While in this mode,

moving the cursor away would hide
the panel after a brief amount of time.

Note that the pop-up and hide delay
is controlled in the preferences
under the System branch
in the View page.

In the bottom right
corner of Altium Designer

click on Panels
and select Storage Manager
to open the Storage Manager panel.
By default, this is a floating panel

and is useful
when explaining the floating display mode.

A panel in this mode can be placed
anywhere within or outside
the Altium Designer environment.

For example,
the Components panel is commonly made

to be floating
and placed on another monitor.
Close the Storage Manager panel.
As you can see, the projects,
navigator, and SCH filter panels

are grouped together
into one panel on the left.
To open any of them

click on the tabs
at the bottom of the panel.
This is what we refer to as
“tabbed panel grouping”.

Close any panel by right-clicking
on its title bar
or on its tab.
Then choose Close from the pop-up menu.

Alternatively, if you want to close
a group of tabbed panels,

you can click the close icon at the top right
of the panel's caption bar.
The panel arrangements
are what we refer to as “desktop layouts”.
Desktop layouts can be saved,

loaded, and reset to default
in the Preferences

from the upper right corner
of Altium Designer.
Open the System branch
and open the view page.
Within the Desktop section,

desktop layouts can be saved, loaded,
and reset to default.
Click on Reset.
Close any panels that open automatically.
Then click OK to exit the Preferences.

In this video,
we explored how documents and panels

can be used to organize and manage
the design workspace in Altium Designer.

title: Altium Training - Design Environment: Documents and Panels
